summary: Eareckson Air Station is a remote military airfield situated on Shemya Island in Alaska's far-western Aleutian Island chain, making it one of the westernmost airports in the United States. Originally established during World War II as Shemya Army Airfield, it was renamed in 1993 in honor of Captain William O. Eareckson, a B-17 pilot killed in a 1943 crash on the island. Today it serves as a strategic diversion airfield for transpacific flights and is operated primarily by the Alaska Air National Guard.
faqs:
Q: Where is Eareckson Air Station located?
A: It is located on Shemya Island, part of the Near Islands group in the Aleutian Island chain of Alaska, near the western tip of the U.S.

Q: Is Eareckson Air Station open to commercial passengers?
A: No, it is primarily a military installation and does not offer scheduled commercial passenger service. Access is restricted to authorized personnel and emergency transpacific diversions.

Q: Why is this airport strategically important?
A: Its remote mid-Pacific position makes it a critical emergency diversion airfield for aircraft crossing the Pacific Ocean between North America and Asia.

Q: What is the runway configuration at SYA?
A: The station features a single long runway, approximately 10,000 feet in length, capable of handling large military and commercial aircraft.
transport_tips: Civilian access is extremely limited; travel to Shemya Island typically requires military transport or chartered aircraft from Anchorage via the Aleutian Island chain. There are no public roads, ferries, or commercial terminals serving the island. All personnel must arrange clearance through the Alaska Air National Guard or sponsoring military unit in advance.
local_tip: Due to its extreme remoteness and harsh subarctic maritime climate, visitors should prepare for rapidly changing weather, frequent fog, and high winds—and always carry more than the recommended survival gear, as resupply options on Shemya are virtually nonexistent.
